brief.headline: Push price toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc (market says ₹0.55–1.20, typical ₹0.85–0.95) and qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source — their finances aren't public, so lean on our ₹63.21 L spend and strong alternates.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for pricing in the ₹0.65–0.80/pc range for 28 mm caps
priceAsk.basis: Open-market asks for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps run ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The market verdict says MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec. We buy ₹63.21 L a year — that's volume they want to keep.

paymentTermAsk.summary: No change needed — already at 30 Days After Receipt, which is standard

brief.financialLeverage: Bprex publishes no financials, so we can't see their profit, debt or cash position. That means we build our ask around what we do know: we spend ₹63.21 L a year with them — real money for a private converter — and we have four strong alternates (Manjushree at ₹2569.83 Cr, Mold-Tek at ₹946.50 Cr, Hitech at ₹701.17 Cr, plus Pearl). Without their numbers, the plan is straightforward: push price toward the lower end of the market band using our volume, and start qualifying a second source in parallel so we're not reliant on one supplier whose finances we can't see.

risks: Bprex's finances aren't public — we can't see if they're healthy or stretched, so watch for any signs of delivery slip or quality issues that might flag trouble

We have no internal price benchmark (no bestPriceWePay) for rigid plastic packaging — the market ask is our only yardstick, so validate it with a quick RFQ to Manjushree or Mold-Tek before you lock the target
If Bprex pushes back hard on price, it may signal they're already thin on margin — don't squeeze so hard that you lose the supplier before the second source is qualified

brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership and want to keep growing together — and to do that, we need pricing that matches what the market supports, which is ₹0.65–0.80 for the volumes we're doing with you.
